About Us

For 40 years, Encore Corporate Travel has helped CFOs, CPOs, and travel leaders reimagine business travel-simpler, smarter, and more personal.

With 24/7 Traveler Services, proprietary technology, proactive program management, and integrated Meetings & Events, Encore delivers clarity, control, and care across every experience.

As a proudly woman-owned, independent company, Encore moves fast, solves harder problems, and grows with intention, never compromising on the personalized service that sets it apart.

A VIP travelerdoes not want to be asked twice.

The windowseat booked without a reminder. The hotel loyalty number applied before theythink to mention it. The connection they hate, avoided on instinct becausesomeone remembered the last three times it went wrong. That is not service.That is being known, and it is the difference between an agent and a resource.

VIP CorporateTravel Agents at Encore exist because being known does not happen by accident.Dedicated and complex accounts do not land with this role because policyrequires it. They land because the traveler learned, itinerary after itinerary,that their preferences are never an afterthought here.

The Role

As a VIP Corporate Travel Agent, you manage new bookings and changes across air, hotel, rail, and car for Encore's most demanding travel clients: name changes, date shifts, itinerary rebuilds, all handled inside the client's travel policy and inside the traveler's expectations. You carry sensitive, private information with the same care every time, not just when someone is watching.
This is not a booking role. It is a relationship role wearing an agent's title.
What You'll Do

Own every VIP itinerary, start to finish. You book and rebuild international air, hotel, rail, and car reservations, and you do it fluently in the loyalty programs that matter to the traveler holding the ticket.
Protect what's sensitive and keep it compliant. You complete document verification and pre-check for every traveler in your care, advise on entry requirements before they're asked about, and keep every reservation inside the client's policy without being told twice.
Anticipate before they ask. You learn each traveler's preferences and hold them across every booking. An air request with a night away from home is an opening to offer the right hotel, not an afterthought. You close the loop other agents leave open.
Raise the standard for the team. You're a resource to your colleagues, not just your travelers. You answer questions before they're fully asked, and you share the tips and tricks that turn a good file into a clean one. Dedicated and complex accounts land with you because that reputation is earned, one file at a time.

Requirements
What You Bring

Required

• Extensivetravel industry experience (20+ years), with demonstrated expertise in US domestic travel, international itineraries, fare rules, and loyalty program mechanics

• Fluent written and verbal communication skills in English

• Advanced, current knowledge of travel industry rules and processes, including document requirements and entry rules that shift by destination

• The soft skills to guide a traveler to resolution in the fewest exchanges possible, and the persuasive, precise writing to do the same with colleagues and other teams

• A customer orientation strong enough to build lasting relationships with travelers who do not tolerate friction

• Ownership of mistakes: you correct them without waiting to be asked

• The organizational discipline to manage multiple complex or dedicated accounts at once without missing a detail, and to meet service level agreements on every interaction

An asset

• Deep knowledge of US-based corporate travel programs and compliance requirements

We’re on the lookout for smart, savvy, and curious Generative AI Specialist to join our global contributor community as part of our Subject Matter Expert (SME) on Demand program.
This is not a traditional full-time role. It’s a part-time, remote, flexible, project-specific opportunity designed for those who want to make a real impact-on their schedule. Whether you're a writer, linguist, educator, researcher, or just deeply passionate about language and logic, this role lets you contribute to cutting-edge AI development while maintaining control over your time.
You’ll be helping LLMs learn the intricacies of language and reasoning-not just how to write, but how to think. If you’ve ever dreamed of shaping the intelligence behind tomorrow’s technology, this is your chance.
This is more than just a gig-it’s a rare chance to help shape the future of AI from anywhere in the world, on your own terms.
What You’ll Own:

• Rating/assessing the performance of AI models or algorithms based on their output or behavior through a set of evaluative questions.

• Labeling elements of a piece of content rather than the content as a whole.

• Assigning predefined categories or labels to items.

• Evaluating the perceived quality and/or appropriateness of content

• Generating labels to advance understanding of a concept, trend etc.

• Creation of additional training data for machine learning models by applying transformations to the original data, such as modifying images (rotation, flipping, cropping), generating new text (paraphrasing, summarization), or altering audio/video signals (speed modification, pitch shifting) to reduce overfitting and increase dataset diversity.

• Reviewing data and identifying whether or not a product feature works as intended based on the project's guidelines.

• Labeling model outputs to identify if a piece of content is or isn't something. Examples: identify clickbait; identifying gaming videos; identifying branded content.

• Ordering or ranking items based on a set of preferences or criteria.

• Creating prompts or questions that will be used to generate responses from a language model or other AI system.

• Projects that evaluate the relevance of content based on a relevancy scale (1-3, 1-5, etc.).

• Generating responses to prompts or questions using a language model or other AI system.

• Rewriting existing text while preserving the original meaning, often to improve clarity or style and adherence to guidelines.

• Producing concise summaries of longer pieces of text or data.

• Converting spoken language or audio content into written text.

• Converting text or spoken language from one language to another.

• Gathering and compiling various forms of data to be used for training, evaluating, or fine-tuning the AI models. This may include text, images, videos, audio files, or other types of digital content.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

• A Bachelor’s degree or higher in a humanities specialization is required. Advanced degrees are strongly preferred (Master’s or PhD)

• Professional or Expert level proficiency (C1/C2) in English

title: SAP Developer
description:
This is a remote position.
Position Overview
We are looking for an experienced SAP Developer with strong hands-on expertise in SAP Security and SAP Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC). The ideal candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, configuring, and maintaining SAP security roles, access controls, authorization objects, and GRC solutions to ensure secure and compliant access across SAP applications.
The role will support enterprise ERP transformation initiatives, security enhancements, access governance, and ongoing production support. The candidate will work closely with functional teams, business stakeholders, internal audit, and compliance teams to implement effective security controls, minimize access risks, and maintain compliance with organizational policies and audit requirements.
Key Responsibilities
SAP Security & Authorization Development

• Design, develop, configure, and maintain SAP security roles, composite roles, derived roles, and authorization profiles.

• Manage user provisioning, role assignments, authorization objects, and access requests across SAP environments.

• Work with SAP authorization concepts, including PFCG, SU24, SU01, SU53, and ST01, to troubleshoot and resolve authorization issues.

• Support SAP ECC and/or SAP S/4HANA security, including SAP Fiori applications, catalogs, groups, and authorization roles, as applicable.

• Perform role modifications, security testing, transport management, and deployment of security changes across development, quality assurance, and production environments.

• Analyze authorization failures and implement appropriate fixes while following change management procedures.

SAP GRC & Access Control

•
Configure, enhance, and support SAP GRC Access Control solutions, including:

• ARA (Access Risk Analysis): Identify and analyze Segregation of Duties (SoD) conflicts, critical access risks, and sensitive permissions.

• ARM (Access Request Management): Manage and configure access request workflows, approvals, and provisioning processes.

• EAM (Emergency Access Management): Administer Firefighter access, controller assignments, usage logs, and review processes.

• BRM (Business Role Management): Support business role definition, role lifecycle management, and governance.

• Maintain and customize SoD rulesets, risk definitions, functions, and mitigation controls.

• Perform access risk analysis, role simulations, and remediation of identified security conflicts.

• Support User Access Reviews (UAR), periodic access certifications, and emergency access reviews.

• Troubleshoot GRC workflow, integration, provisioning, and authorization issues.

Compliance, Audit & Risk Management

• Support SOX-related controls, internal audits, external audits, and compliance assessments where applicable.

• Maintain evidence for access reviews, role approvals, emergency access usage, and security changes.

• Ensure appropriate segregation between business-critical activities and sensitive transactions.

• Identify opportunities to strengthen access governance and reduce security risks.

• Collaborate with auditors and business process owners to resolve findings and implement corrective actions.

Development, Integration & Production Support

• Analyze security requirements and translate them into technical configurations and development specifications.

• Support security integration with connected SAP applications and identity or provisioning systems, where applicable.

• Work with SAP technical and functional teams to resolve access issues affecting business processes such as finance, procurement, inventory, order management, and supply chain.

• Participate in system upgrades, ERP implementations, security testing, cutover activities, and post-go-live stabilization.

• Follow ITSM processes for incident, problem, change, and release management.

• Maintain technical documentation, configuration records, and operational procedures.

Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed - we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. CrowdStrike's cybersecurity data is one-of-a-kind: we process nearly a trillion behavioral events per day. title: Lead Designer, Digital Experience Standards
description:
About the Team/Role:
As the Lead Designer for Digital Experience Standards at WEX Inc., you will set and hold the bar for experience quality across our digital portfolio and codify it through scalable platforms. Reporting to the Director of Digital Platforms & Practice, you are a senior individual contributor accountable for how our products look, sound, and feel as more of the experience is generated by agents rather than assembled by hand.

This is a “tastemaker” role. We define taste as the ability to draw from deep customer empathy, consider your product’s brand tone, voice, and identity, and channel them into an end-to-end experience that is consistent, recognizable, seamless, and delightful. As AI collapses the cost of producing an interface, taste becomes the constraint that matters-and the difference between a portfolio that feels intentional and one that merely functions.

This role sits within WEX’s centralized digital standards and practices group. While design teams are aligned to individual product lines, this position connects that work through shared standards, design systems, and AI-enabled practices. You will influence quality across dozens of web and mobile experiences, partner with the branding team, and coach designers rather than own a single product’s roadmap.

If you hold strong opinions about craft, have an instinct for what customers feel but do not say, and can encode that judgment so other people-and agents-apply it at scale, this is the role for you.
What You’ll Do:

•
Set Experience Standards & Taste: Define what “good” looks like across the portfolio and encode it as standards, patterns, and reference examples that any designer or agent can apply without you in the room.

•
Make Coherence Scalable: Build a system in which experiences feel recognizably WEX in brand, tone, voice, and interaction regardless of which team or agent produced them.

•
Lead Portfolio-Level Critique: Lead critique and calibration that builds judgment in other designers and raises craft rather than policing it.

•
Anticipate Emerging Modalities: Bring a point of view on voice, conversational, and multimodal interaction so standards anticipate how customers will work rather than how they have worked.

•
Own the Design OS for the Agentic Lifecycle: Own the reusable components, skills, standards, and machine-readable context that agents invoke to generate consistent UI in ADLC Foundations Hub and Discovery & Delivery Systems.

•
Translate Design Intent into Build-Ready Artifacts: Partner with the design system engineer to create tokens, patterns, schemas, and documentation that both humans and agents can consume.

•
Make Quality the Default: Make the standard the path of least resistance, so generated experiences inherit accessibility, usability, and brand quality by default rather than by review.

•
Use AI-Assisted Coding and Prototyping: Use modern AI-assisted coding and prototyping tools to explore concepts, test interactions, and operationalize repeatable design guidance. Tools discussed for this role include Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex.

•
Define Experience Quality Measurement: Establish an enterprise experience quality rubric with dimensions, criteria, and severity scales for usability, accessibility, brand and voice coherence, language clarity, and end-to-end journey quality.

•
Build Agentic Evaluation at Scale: Develop evaluation capabilities that allow agents to navigate live customer portals, mobile apps, and internal tools across full journeys and return evidence-backed findings.

•
Make Quality Visible to Leadership: Produce a portfolio-level experience quality index and heat map showing strengths, weaknesses, and specific quality dimensions across lines of business.

•
Connect Quality to Business Outcomes: Correlate experience quality with NPS, CSAT, and customer trust measures, and use those signals to direct standards, coaching, and investment toward experiences where customer risk is highest.

The insights you gather from your customers will directly inform our research priorities, product development, and go-to-market strategies. As one of the founding members of our Customer Success team in Japan, you'll help shape how we build the function in-region. The role requires understanding of markets, exchange products, and order-book dynamics, alongside sound judgment. You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, Risk, Central Compliance, and local Compliance teams to support a robust and continuously improving surveillance framework. You will maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready investigation records, while contributing to special projects and priority requests in a fast-paced global environment.

•
Investigate potential market abuse activity, including wash trading, circular trading, price ramping, insider trading, spoofing, layering, and other related activities.

•
Review and analyze surveillance alerts using industry-leading tools and platforms.

•
Produce thorough, high-quality investigations supported by clear evidence and well-documented conclusions.

•

title: Staff Software Development Engineer - Windows Endpoint
description:
Diversity. Inclusion. They’re more than just words for us. They are the guiding values of how we build our teams, cultivate leaders, and create a culture where people feel connected.
We take care of our employees so they can take care of our customers. Customers who come from all walks of life just like us. We hire incredible people from diverse backgrounds because when we are different together, we are stronger together.
The Role
As Staff Software Development Engineer, you'll be the Windows kernel authority for the runtime enforcement layer of our Identity Security Platform. These components decide, in-kernel, whether to permit or deny each action an identity or AI agent attempts on a Windows endpoint.
You'll set the technical direction for kernel-mode enforcement on Windows and own it end to end. That means hooks that make the right call in real time, across the fleet, without breaking legitimate workloads. Peer engineers own the macOS and Linux enforcement surfaces. You share one policy language, one event schema, and one userspace agent with them, but Windows kernel-space is yours.
You know this layer better than anyone. You want your code to be the thing that stops a compromised credential or a runaway AI coding agent before it impacts production.
What You’ll Do

• Design, build, and own our kernel-mode enforcement drivers: file-system, process and thread creation, handle operations, and registry access. You'll block operations inline in the kernel rather than logging them after the fact, and you'll build the userspace agent that installs and drives them.

• Own the kernel/user-mode enforcement boundary: kernel-side event capture, policy evaluation in user mode, and deny decisions pushed back into the driver as hash-keyed caches so subsequent hits block inline.

• Drive down enforce-mode latency on the operation hot path as we scale across large fleets. That means process enrichment, image-hash caching and eviction under heavy process-churn, and process-ancestry resolution across PPID spoofing.

• Extend enforcement into containers and isolation: Windows containers and Host Compute Service workloads, silo- and job-object-aware policy, and container identity on kernel events. Most of this is greenfield, and it sits at the center of the role.

• Harden portability and stability across Windows builds so enforcement loads and behaves correctly on the versions customers actually run. You'll deal with structure-versioning across Windows releases, PatchGuard constraints, Driver Verifier and HVCI compliance, WHQL attestation signing, and graceful degradation when a capability isn't available.

• Partner with the Linux and macOS enforcement engineers and the policy-backend team on the shared plane: policy semantics, cross-stack conformance, event schema, the common Rust agent. You'll represent Windows in cross-org architecture reviews.

• Read requirements to find gaps and risks, propose simplifications, and explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Raise the engineering bar. You'll take end-to-end ownership from design through production, and you'll carry extra weight where a kernel bug means a wrong security decision or a bugcheck across the fleet, not just a crash of one process.

• Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on Windows systems and kernel-driver craft.

What You’ll Bring
This is a Windows specialist role, so the depth requirements are real:

• Deep Windows kernel internals - the I/O manager and IRP flow, the object manager, process and thread structures, memory management, the Windows security model (tokens, SIDs, ACLs) - backed by production kernel-mode driver development in C, C++, or Rust.

• Hands-on kernel-mode driver work for security enforcement. You've shipped a file-system minifilter or comparable callback-based driver, and you can reason about IRQL, synchronization, safe user-buffer access, and reentrancy in the kernel. The Problem We're Hiring You to Solve
Monthly production releases. Zero escaped critical defects. Most engineering organizations treat those as a tradeoff. On this program they are both commitments, measured every release, in front of the customer.
We are hiring the engineering leader who builds an organization that delivers both at once: multiple cross-functional development teams modernizing a federal home loan benefit platform while sustaining the 20-year-old system it replaces. If you believe speed and quality are the same discipline practiced well, and you have the delivery record to prove it, keep reading.
The Opportunity
Most engineering leadership roles ask you to protect a delivery machine someone else built. This one asks you to build the machine.
The program spans multiple development teams working in parallel across a modern platform (Salesforce-centered, configuration-first, supplemented by serverless capabilities in a government cloud) and a legacy suite that must stay stable until it is decommissioned. Work arrives through a formal intake process that turns business needs into executable plans with committed scope, timelines, and team sizing in days. Then your organization delivers against those commitments, publicly and measurably.
The quality bar is unusually explicit. Every release ships with 100% automated test coverage for its features before user acceptance testing begins. Defect detection before UAT must exceed 95%. Escaped critical defects must be zero. Critical production bugs get fixed in three days. Accessibility and security compliance are release gates, not aspirations. These are not stretch goals on a slide. They are how the program measures the engineering organization every month.
That bar is exactly why this role is interesting. Hitting it once takes heroics. Hitting it every month takes an engineering system: disciplined definition of done, test automation as a first-class craft, engineers who own quality instead of throwing code over a wall, and a leader who builds all of that into how teams work rather than inspecting it in afterward. That leader is you.
You will work alongside a Senior DevSecOps & Platform Engineering Lead who owns the delivery pipeline and an Enterprise Solution Architect who owns the designs. You own the organization that turns those designs into shipped, tested, production software.

• The engineering organization. Lead multiple cross-functional development teams across modern and legacy platforms, flexing team size and composition as workflows through intake. Teams form, deliver, and re-form around the work. You make that fluid instead of chaotic.

• Delivery you put your name on. Commit to scope, level of effort, and timelines in executable plans, then hit them. When you cannot, say so early, with a recovery plan, before the customer discovers it.

• A quality system, not a QA gate. Engineer quality into how teams work: definition of done that includes full automated testing, code review that catches problems, and metrics that surface risk early. The outcomes that prove it: zero escaped critical defects, defect detection above 95% before UAT, and critical fixes inside three days.

• Test automation as a craft. Build the discipline where every feature ships with complete positive and negative automated coverage, and the regression suite becomes the safety net the customer trusts enough to focus UAT on new functionality only.

• The monthly release drumbeat. Production value ships every 30 days or faster, release after release, without burning the team down to do it.

Full-time, remote. Must be available during core business hours (Eastern Time) to support stakeholder calls and submission deadlines. Occasional travel may be required.

$115,000 to $140,000 annually, commensurate with experience

Position Overview:

AptNexus is seeking a Senior Cybersecurity Compliance Analyst to support a cybersecurity compliance program for our Department of Treasury customer. The program oversees the protection of sensitive federal data held by federal, state, and local government organizations, which submit corrective action plans, system security plans, technical inquiries, and change notifications for review. In this role, you will evaluate these submissions against security requirements tailored from NIST SP 800-53 and deliver clear, well-supported compliance determinations and guidance. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented self-starter who can manage a steady volume of reviews with consistency and precision.

Duties/Responsibilities:

• Evaluate corrective action plans and POA&Ms submitted by partner organizations, including supporting evidence such as screenshots, audit logs, and policy documents, and determine whether each finding is open or closed.

• Recommend specific follow-on actions required to close open findings, and address questions and statements raised in partner organization responses.

• Review system security plans and related compliance submissions against applicable NIST controls, clearly identify compliance status, and articulate applicable requirements.

• Prepare written responses to technical inquiries on topics such as multifactor authentication, cloud configuration, and control implementation methodologies, and conduct follow-up calls as needed.

• Evaluate advance notifications of planned changes, such as cloud adoption, contractor access, and test environments, and provide written cybersecurity guidance.

• Perform quality reviews of audit reports and remediation tracking documentation before delivery to the customer.

• Manage the submission review queue, tracking volumes, due dates, and turnaround to meet customer deadlines.

• Develop and maintain automated tools, such as Excel VBA macros and standardized templates, to improve the consistency and efficiency of reviews.

• Review the work of other analysts for accuracy and consistency, and provide technical guidance on complex determinations.

• Maintain complete and accurate records of all correspondence and documentation in the customer’s case management system.

• Contribute recommendations to improve review procedures, templates, and guidance.

• Comply with all customer security, privacy, and records management requirements, using only Government-furnished equipment and approved systems.

Required Skills

• Minimum of seven (7) years of cybersecurity experience, including at least five (5) years in federal cybersecurity compliance, audit, or assessment, with direct experience evaluating POA&Ms or system security plans.

• Expert working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 (moderate and high baselines), the NIST Risk Management Framework, NIST SP 800-30, and FIPS, including the ability to evaluate compliance against control sets tailored from NIST.

• Test operating-system updates, security patches, vendor patches, and application updates before production deployment.

• Monitor deployment progress, failure

title: Security Systems Administrator
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE SECURITY TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- You're securing the frontier of AI. The model weights training on our infrastructure are the most valuable and most targeted artifacts in technology, and we're standing up the compute to hold them faster than anyone ever has. A breach isn't a leak, it's the frontier walking out the door.

- Build the entire security program from scratch. Most leaders inherit someone else's system and spend a career patching it. Here you own it end to end, bare metal to boardroom, as we scale across continents.

- The industry's playbook was written for one building at a time. Vendor-managed appliances, manual process, and standards that assume a security team walks the floor. None of that survives contact with what we're building, so we build what should exist rather than buying what does.

- Your threat surface is measured in gigawatts. The customers running on our infrastructure are building the most consequential technology in human history, and being responsible for the physical and logical security of that work makes everything else feel small.

ROLE SCOPE

- Define the acceptance criteria that decide whether a building enters support, and hold that gate while campuses across multiple gigawatt-scale sites move toward turnover faster than any conventional operations model was built to absorb.

- Run the device remediation queue across cameras, readers, and controllers to the response and resolution targets in the support agreement, on an estate that grows every quarter.

- Execute firmware and patch cycles across a fleet spanning multiple gigawatt-scale campuses without taking video or access control offline.

- Lead technical incident response when the system itself fails, and drive vendor and integrator break/fix to closure rather than waiting on it.

- Throw out the parts of conventional physical security operations that only survive because nobody questioned them, starting with manual device inventories, truck rolls for work that should be remote, and documentation that goes stale the day it ships.

- Write runbooks and standards that hold at every site, so the next campus costs the team tooling rather than headcount.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

title: 3D Artist (Blender & Real-Time Specialist)
description:
Job Spec: 3D Artist (Blender & Real-Time Specialist)

Location: Remote

Reporting to: Creative Director

The Role

We are looking for a versatile and technically proficient 3D Artist to join our growing creative team. You will be responsible for bringing complex concepts to life through high-quality modeling and fluid animation, primarily using Blender. As we specialize in interactive web-based demos, your primary challenge will be the "magic trick" of 3D: making assets look like high-end cinema while keeping them lightweight enough to load

instantly in a mobile browser. You will work under our Creative Director and alongside our development team to bridge the gap between high-fidelity art and web performance.

Key Responsibilities

• Modeling & Texturing: Create high-quality 3D assets optimized for performance. This includes expert-level retopology and baking high-to-low poly details.

• Animation: Develop smooth, purposeful animations-ranging from mechanical movements to

environmental storytelling-using Blender’s animation suite.

• Web Optimization: Ensure all assets are "game-ready" for the browser, focusing on low draw calls, efficient texture atlasing, and minimal file sizes.

• Collaboration: Work alongside other 3D artists and frontend developers to ensure visual consistency and technical compatibility.

• Pipeline Integration: Prepare and export assets (primarily glTF/GLB) that are ready for immediate implementation into our interactive platforms.

Technical Requirements

• Blender Mastery: Advanced proficiency in modeling, retopology, rigging, shading, and animation.

• Real-Time Optimization: Proven experience creating assets for web-based engines (Three.js, Babylon.js, or PlayCanvas). You should be an expert in:

○ Polygon Budgeting: Keeping mesh density low without losing silhouette.

○ Texture Compression: Efficient use of 1k/2k textures and PBR workflows.

○ Draw Call Reduction: Merging meshes and materials strategically.

• Visual Flair: A strong portfolio demonstrating a mastery of lighting and material creation.

Bonus Points

• Development Experience: Experience working directly within a dev sprint, using version control (Git), or understanding the limitations of WebGL.

• Technical Art: Knowledge of Python scripting within Blender to automate export pipelines.

• Material Science: Experience with KHR extensions for glTF (clearcoat, transmission, sheen) to achieve high-end looks in the browser.

Why Us?

We create virtual instrument simulations for lab equipment - helping people learn and service. We work with global biotech companies and we are always pushing boundaries with technical and creative ideas.

title: SEM Technician (f/m/d)
description:
Your Role

As an SEM Technician (f/m/d), you will support tools and process qualifications and help investigate issues arising across our semiconductor process flow. Working closely with our Failure Analysis Engineer, Process Integration team and other engineering functions, you will perform Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) analysis and complementary characterization using techniques such as Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX) and Focused Ion Beam (FIB).

Ideally you come with a first-hand experience working with SEM. You will initially work alongside our SEM experts to deepen your knowledge learn the tool’s operating principles, procedures and inspection requirements for our specific use cases. Through hands-on training and continuous knowledge transfer, you will build your skills in sample handling, imaging, measurement and troubleshooting; before gradually becoming an independent SEM user and taking greater ownership of the tool and the processes.

As the function develops, there may also be opportunities to operate additional defect-inspection tools and support defect analysis and yield improvement within our 300 mm manufacturing facility.

What You’ll Do

- Prepare, handle and inspect a wide range of semiconductor samples according to defined analysis requirements

- Perform accurate and reliable SEM analysis to support tool qualification, process qualification and root-cause investigations

- Use complementary characterization techniques, including EDX and FIB, where required

- Work closely with Failure Analysis, Process Integration and engineering teams to understand inspection requirements and communicate results effectively across functions

- Maintain accurate records of incoming sample lots, expected outcomes, reporting deadlines and priorities

- Perform daily, weekly and monthly tool-health checks, calibration and routine performance monitoring

- Troubleshoot tool and measurement issues and coordinate with equipment vendors to maintain tool availability

- Maintain an accurate inventory of consumables and spare parts required for reliable SEM operation

- Standardize measurement procedures and reporting methods to ensure consistent and repeatable results

- Document operating procedures and best practices and, over time, support the training of additional SEM operators

- Support the operation of additional defect-inspection tools and contribute to defect analysis and yield-improvement activities as the team grows

What You Bring

- Technical training or a bachelor’s or master’s degree in physics, chemistry, engineering, materials science or a related field

- Previous hands-on experience operating SEM systems

- Experience with FIB and EDX is highly desirable

- An understanding of sample preparation, imaging, measurement and basic failure-analysis methods

- Previous experience working in a semiconductor cleanroom is an advantage

- Willingness and ability to spend extended periods working in a cleanroom while wearing the required PPE

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to work carefully and consistently with sensitive samples and equipment

- A structured approach to documentation, sample tracking and task prioritization

- Confidence working in a dynamic environment with interconnected technical dependencies and changing priorities

- Good communication skills in English, with a reliable, open and honest approach to working with stakeholders

- Willingness to learn, take increasing ownership and support tasks beyond your immediate scope when needed

title: Medical Chart Reviewer
description:
Role Title: Medical Chart Reviewer
Role Type: Contractor
Location : US - Remote
micro1 is engaging Medical Chart Reviewers (CCS / CIC / CPC certified, or RN / clinical background) to contribute their expertise to a dynamic project for a valued customer. In this role, you’ll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required, your domain knowledge is what matters.
Scope of Work

• Review and audit medical charts, including admission notes, progress notes, operative reports, consults, lab and imaging results, and discharge summaries, to verify the accuracy and completeness of documentation and assigned codes.

• Validate diagnosis and procedure coding, sequencing, Present on Admission (POA) indicators, and MS-DRG assignment against the clinical documentation, identifying under-coding, over-coding, and missed CCs and MCCs.

• Apply clinical and coding standards, including the ICD-10-CM/PCS Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting, AHA Coding Clinic guidance, and clinical validation criteria, while flagging documentation gaps and query opportunities.

• Collaborate with project stakeholders using both written and verbal communication to clarify requirements, resolve documentation ambiguities, and ensure data integrity.

• Deliver high-quality feedback on charts, coding guidelines, and complex cases to support project workflow improvements and enhance AI model understanding.

• Ensure accuracy and completeness of all review findings per current best practices and coding standards.

Preferred Qualifications

• Active AHIMA Certified Coding Specialist (CCS), AAPC Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC), AAPC Certified Professional Coder (CPC), or an RN / clinical credential with chart review or CDI experience.

• Thorough expertise in ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and MS-DRG methodology, with hands-on experience in chart review, coding audit, or clinical documentation improvement (CDI).

• Experience reviewing charts in diverse settings, such as acute care, teaching hospitals, specialty units, surgical, trauma, oncology, cardiology, and transplant cases.

• Proficiency in reviewing various types of clinical documentation and identifying discrepancies or complex coding challenges.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, demonstrating meticulous attention to detail and clarity.

• Access to current ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS code sets, Official Coding Guidelines, and MS-DRG grouper tools.

title: Channel Enablement Manager
description:
About the Role

Through the channel, a great product only wins when the partner knows how to sell it. At Abnormal, we want every partner ready to lead with the whole platform.

Abnormal is a channel-first company: nearly all of our transactions run through partners, which makes partner readiness a direct driver of revenue. As Channel Enablement Manager, you will own how our reseller, distributor, and referral partners learn to position, sell, and support the full Abnormal platform, and how our internal sellers work alongside them. We are expanding from email security into a multi-product behavioral platform spanning Identity, Insider Risk, and AI Security, so partners need to lead with the platform and grow every customer over time. You will be the person who makes that possible.

This is a high-visibility individual contributor role on the Sales Enablement team, working closely with Channel Leadership, Channel Account Managers (CAMs), and Channel SEs. You will build scalable, role-based partner enablement and certifications, deliver training people remember, and use data to prove that enabled partners generate more pipeline and win more deals. It is a role for someone who loves the craft of helping others succeed and wants to bring AI to the center of how enablement scales.

What You Will Do

• Build the framework. Design, build, and deliver a role-based partner enablement framework (Partner Essentials, Partner Sales 101, Pre-Sales 101, and advanced modules) through the Partner Portal and live sessions.

• Get partners productive faster. Lead partner onboarding that takes new and focus partners from signed to productive, with clear readiness milestones and certification paths.

• Train with impact. Deliver engaging in-person and virtual training to partner sellers, SEs, and leaders on Abnormal's value proposition, SEG displacement, discovery, qualification, and competitive positioning.

• Prepare our own teams to co-sell. Enable Abnormal AEs, SDRs, and SEs on how to work with partners, including rules of engagement, deal registration, channel discounts, and renewal incumbency.

• Create the assets partners use. Partner with CAMs, Channel SEs, Channel Ops, Channel Marketing, and Product Marketing to deliver partner-facing sales plays, use cases, win wires, campaigns-in-a-box, and competitive intelligence.

• Let the data steer. Use performance data (partner-sourced pipeline, deal reg conversion, certification completion, win rates) to find gaps, prioritize investments, and report measurable impact.

• Scale with AI. Use AI to scale enablement and reduce CAM 1:1 training time, through AI-assisted content, roleplays, and on-demand coaching, so CAMs can focus on pipeline generation and partner-sourced revenue.

Must Haves

• 5 to 8+ years in channel sales, partner management, sales, or a sales-supporting role (for example, channel/partner enablement, CAM, channel SE, sales enablement), with a track record of individual success and/or developing others.

• Direct experience working with or enabling channel partners (VARs, resellers, distributors, MSPs, or referral partners) in a B2B SaaS environment, a solid understanding of how partners make money and decide which vendors to champion, and the credibility to influence partner sellers and internal AEs on co-selling, deal registration, and channel conflict.

• Experience designing and running scalable enablement: certifications, on-demand courses, LMS/partner portal content, and live training.

• A genuine desire to help others succeed, with a sense of accomplishment tied to partner and field performance as much as your own.

• A strong analytical mindset. You use data to diagnose performance and prioritize enablement, and can describe past examples of how data drove change.

title: Product Manager, Pricing and Monetization
description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

PRODUCT AT BASETEN

Baseten is building a new cloud for AI. Our ambition is to make inference, training, and agent execution part of one coherent platform, and to shape how the next generation of AI products gets built. Product decisions here reach from the economics of GPU infrastructure to the abstractions developers build on every day.

We’re hiring builders and tastemakers with the ambition to help create that future. You should bring a strong point of view about what should exist, the taste to make complex technology feel simple, and the technical judgment to build it alongside engineers, researchers, and designers. You’ll work directly with customers and forward deployed teams, turn emerging capabilities into new possibilities for developers, and carry an idea from early conviction through to production and adoption.

THE ROLE

Shape how AI infrastructure is priced, packaged, and sold.

AI infrastructure is changing fast, and the way customers pay for it is evolving just as quickly. Tokens, GPUs, reserved capacity, training jobs, agent execution. Different workloads have different economics, and traditional cloud pricing models don't always fit.

We're looking for a Product Manager to lead pricing and monetization across Baseten's platform.

You'll help determine how we package our products, measure usage, price new capabilities, and make it easier for customers to understand and manage their spend.

This is a rare opportunity to influence both how customers experience our platform and how the business grows.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own pricing and packaging strategy across inference, training, sandboxes, Grid, and future products.

- Design pricing models for token-based inference, dedicated deployments, reserved capacity, and emerging AI workloads.

- Work with engineering and finance to understand infrastructure costs, GPU utilization, margins, and usage patterns.

- Build and test pricing strategies using customer research, quantitative analysis, and real-world usage data.

- Shape the developer and enterprise purchasing experience, including credits, commitments, discounts, overages, and billing transparency.

- Partner with sales, finance, and product teams to bring pricing changes to market and manage customer transitions.

- Identify opportunities to improve adoption, revenue growth, and unit economics.

REQUIREMENTS

- 10+ years of experience in pricing, packaging, or monetization for cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, or complex usage-based products.

- A track record of owning meaningful pricing decisions, from strategy and modeling through launch and adoption.

- Experience with both self-serve and enterprise pricing, including commitments, consumption models, and commercial negotiations.

- Strong analytical skills, including hands-on work with SQL, financial models, usage data, and customer cohorts.

- A deep understanding of how pricing influences customer behavior, product adoption, and business economics.

- The ability to work across product, engineering, finance, and GTM to turn complex pricing decisions into simple customer experiences.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience pricing AI/ML infrastructure, GPU compute, model APIs, or other emerging developer platforms.

- Familiarity with inference economics, including utilization, caching, retries, and serving costs.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

- Work with Finance, Investor Relations and Communication
